release.md
Deploy migration 002_up.sql first, then replace application instances one at a time. Old and new instances share the database during rollout. Rollback restarts the old binary first, then runs 002_down.sql. Staging has not run this release.

001_initial.sql
CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL);

002_up.sql
ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN name TO display_name;

002_down.sql
ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN display_name TO name;

old_reader.py

new_reader.py

/bin/zsh -lc "git status --short; python3 - <<'PY'
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

files = ['release.md', '001_initial.sql', '002_up.sql', '002_down.sql', 'old_reader.py', 'new_reader.py']
before = {f: hashlib.sha256(Path(f).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for f in files}
readers = {}
for f in ['old_reader.py', 'new_reader.py']:
    tree = ast.parse(Path(f).read_text())
    readers[f] = next(ast.literal_eval(n.value) for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == 'QUERY' for t in n.targets))
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
print('SQLite version:', sqlite3.sqlite_version)

def inspect(state):
    print('\\nSTATE:', state)
    print('schema:', db.execute(\"SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'users'\").fetchone()[0])
    print('rows:', json.dumps(db.execute('SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id').fetchall()))
    for file, query in readers.items():
        try:
            print(file, repr(query), '=>', json.dumps(db.execute(query).fetchall()))
        except sqlite3.Error as e:
            print(file, repr(query), '=> ERROR:', str(e))

db.executescript(Path('001_initial.sql').read_text())
db.executemany('INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES (?, ?)', [(1, 'Alice'), (2, 'Unchanged')])
db.commit()
inspect('initial, seeded existing rows')
db.executescript(Path('002_up.sql').read_text())
inspect('up, before new-schema writes')
print('\\nSynthetic SQL probes only; no application writer was supplied.')
print(\"UPDATE users SET display_name = 'Alice updated' WHERE id = 1\")
db.execute('UPDATE users SET display_name = ? WHERE id = ?', ('Alice updated', 1))
print(\"INSERT INTO users (id, display_name) VALUES (3, 'New user')\")
db.execute('INSERT INTO users (id, display_name) VALUES (?, ?)', (3, 'New user'))
db.commit()
inspect('up, after new-schema insert and update; old binary would restart here per rollback plan')
pre_down = db.execute('SELECT id, display_name FROM users ORDER BY id').fetchall()
db.executescript(Path('002_down.sql').read_text())
inspect('down, after rollback')
post_down = db.execute('SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY id').fetchall()
assert pre_down == post_down
assert post_down == [(1, 'Alice updated'), (2, 'Unchanged'), (3, 'New user')]
print('\\nPASS: updated existing row, unchanged row, and newly inserted row survive down with identical IDs and values.')
after = {f: hashlib.sha256(Path(f).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for f in files}
assert before == after
print('PASS: all six supplied release files remain byte-for-byte unchanged.')
PY"
